title: NY State Assembly · District 58
area: Brooklyn: East Flatbush, Flatlands, Canarsie, and parts of Brownsville

context.text: Incumbent Monique Chandler-Waterman is unopposed in the general election. The Democratic and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled and she advanced on both lines without appearing on the ballot. No Republican candidate filed.

summary.text: Monique Chandler-Waterman is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for Assembly District 58. A community organizer and nonprofit founder, she won a May 2022 special election to succeed N. Nick Perry and is seeking a third full term. She is unopposed in November 2026.

background.text: Chandler-Waterman was born in New York City and graduated from Boys and Girls High School. She earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Berkeley College and a master's degree in business administration from Metropolitan College of New York.
Her career has centered on community organizing and activism; she founded a day care center and co-founded the nonprofit East Flatbush Village, Inc.
She won a May 2022 special election to succeed N. Nick Perry in the Assembly, and was re-elected in the 2022 and 2024 general elections.
For the 2025-2026 session she serves on the Banks, Children and Families, Election Law, Higher Education, Housing, and Mental Health committees.

priorities.text: "Truly affordable housing and policies that protect homeowners from predatory buyers."
"Quality public schools for all students throughout the district."

Police accountability, reflected in her sponsorship of numerous 2025-2026 bills addressing police body-worn cameras, duty-to-intervene requirements, racial profiling in traffic stops, and officer discipline.

positions.summary: Prime sponsor of a bill establishing a state Office of Gun Violence Prevention and a gun violence advisory council.

Prime sponsor of a bill shifting liability for illegal housing-unit conversions from residents to the contractor or building owner, and campaigns on protecting tenants and homeowners from predatory practices.
positions.quote: Truly affordable housing and policies that protect homeowners from predatory buyers

positions.summary: Co-sponsor of the "Fair Share Act," which would authorize an additional 2% New York City income tax on residents, estates, and trusts with more than $1 million in annual taxable income.

record.text: Prime sponsor of A02084, establishing a state Office of Gun Violence Prevention and gun violence advisory council. Referred to the Codes Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A04735 ("Cariol's Law"), creating a duty for police and peace officers to intervene when they see another officer using excessive force. Amended twice and recommitted to the Codes Committee.

Prime sponsor of A07156, providing for indefinite suspension without pay of NYPD officers facing charges of incompetence or misconduct resulting in death or serious physical injury. Referred to the Governmental Employees Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A07202, requiring police and peace officers executing a search warrant to wear an active, unobstructed body camera throughout the search. Referred to the Codes Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A07225, assigning liability for monetary penalties from an illegal housing-unit conversion to the contractor and/or owner rather than the residents. Referred to the Cities Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A07181, defining racial profiling in traffic stops and directing a state study of the practice. Referred to the Governmental Operations Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.
Serves on the Assembly's Banks, Children and Families, Election Law, Higher Education, Housing, and Mental Health committees for the 2025-2026 session.

researchNotes: Chandler-Waterman is unopposed on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot. She has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in any cycle. Her campaign website (moniqueforny.com), used here for priorities, dates to her 2022 campaign and has not been updated with 2026-specific statements; her current legislative record (2025-2026 session), which is documented above, is the more up-to-date source for her priorities and positions.
